questions.question: Which properties are shared across the Inspector's web, CLI, and TUI clients? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: The same transports
The same catalog/config file handling
The same OAuth state on disk
The same protocol-era negotiation (legacy vs modern)
The same flag set — every flag works in all three

questions.explanation: All three are built on one shared core, so transports, config resolution, OAuth state, and era negotiation behave identically. Flags differ per client (e.g., --method is CLI-only, --dev is web-only).

questions.question: Which CLI exit-code interpretations are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: 0 — success
2 — no MCP App found on the tool during an --app-info probe
3 — server requires authentication
4 — server unreachable (DNS, refused, timeout)
5 — usage error (the catch-all)

questions.explanation: 0/2/3/4 are right. Exit 5 means a tool error (isError: true or tool not found); the usage/unexpected catch-all is exit 1.

questions.question: Which statements about --catalog vs --config are true? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: --catalog is writable and is created and seeded if the file doesn't exist
--config is read-only, never written, and errors if the file is missing
The two flags are mutually exclusive
--config files can be edited from the web UI
--catalog defaults to ~/.mcp-inspector/mcp.json (or MCP_CATALOG_PATH)

questions.explanation: A --config file is served as-is and is not editable in the web UI — that's the point of using it for someone else's config. Everything else is accurate.

questions.question: For non-interactive/CI OAuth handling, which CLI flags exist? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: --stored-auth-only — never start interactive OAuth; fail fast if no stored token
--use-stored-auth — reuse (and refresh) a token the web Inspector already obtained
--wait-for-auth <sec> — poll the state file until a token appears
--print-handoff — print the deep link and port-forward command a human needs to complete OAuth remotely
--skip-oauth-forever — permanently disable authorization

questions.explanation: The first four are real flags covering CI and web-to-CLI handoff. There is no --skip-oauth-forever.

questions.question: Which statements about launching the Inspector are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: It runs via npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector with no installation
It requires Node 22.19.0 or newer
The web client prints a URL containing a one-time session token
The web UI listens on 6274 while the CLI/TUI OAuth callback uses 6276
It must be installed globally via npm install -g before first use

questions.explanation: All four launch facts are documented, so the all-of-the-above option is genuinely right.

questions.question: Which combinations or usages do the Inspector docs explicitly forbid or refuse? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Combining DANGEROUSLY_OMIT_AUTH with DANGEROUSLY_BIND_ALL_INTERFACES
Passing --catalog and --config together
Using --method (a CLI flag) on the web client
Running two Inspector instances on one machine
All of the above

questions.explanation: Auth-off plus all-interfaces would expose an unauthenticated proxy to the network, and catalog/config are mutually exclusive; --method is CLI-only. Multiple instances are fine.

questions.question: Which Inspector features help debug the 2026-07-28 protocol era specifically? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A protocol-era selector negotiating auto, modern, or legacy per connection
A populated server/discover view when connected modern
Network-level visibility of the mirrored Mcp-* headers
Rendering of MCP Apps in a sandboxed Apps tab
Built-in load testing to stress-test server capacity

questions.explanation: Era negotiation, discover inspection, header visibility, and the Apps tab are all part of Inspector V2 — E is correct.

questions.question: Which CLI exit-code interpretations are right? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: 0 — success
1 — usage or unexpected error (the catch-all)
3 — the server requires authentication
5 — a tool error (isError: true, or tool not found)
2 — the server is unreachable

questions.explanation: Exit 2 means no MCP App was found during an --app-info probe; unreachable servers exit 4.
